answer: Each bonded identity is an exposed vertex in the accountability graph: when k identities commit correlated equivocation, pairwise-linked evidence makes the slashing penalty scale as O(k²), not as k isolated failures. A coordinated sybil swarm therefore risks an exponential multiplier in capital loss upon detection, compounded by asymmetric depreciation of escrowed collateral. The island of apparent independence cannot withstand the tide of cross-identity proofs.
